caption: The drawing depicts a metal kettle with a rounded body and a tall, curved spout that extends from the left side of the vessel, as seen from the viewer’s perspective. The kettle features a domed lid with a small knob on top at its center and a large, rigid, arched handle attached to the lid area on both sides. The handle has a slightly ornate curve where it meets the kettle. The overall shape of the kettle is asymmetrical, and it appears to have some dents and surface textures suggesting wear. The body and spout are rendered in varying shades of gray and black, giving a metallic and slightly tarnished appearance. In the upper section of the drawing are two smaller schematic diagrams: the first, on the left, shows the kettle in profile (presumably front or back view) as a simple symmetrical oval with short lines indicating dimensions; the second, on the right, is a simple side elevation sketch of the kettle, including its spout, handle, and lid, outlined in black on a white background. The primary drawing of the kettle fills the bottom central part of the page, with fine lines outlining its contours and spots of shading providing volume and texture. The background is an unshaded, plain off-white. Handwritten text in block letters marks the lower left as "GRAPHIC SCALE 1/2" and the lower right as "JOHN L. CUTTING."
title: Copper Kettle
